name: Question 13
problem:
Which of the following are orthogonal projection matrices?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5} & -\frac{2}{5} \\ -\frac{2}{5} & \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5} & -\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{3}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & \frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{3}{4} & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
Recall that $Q$ is an orthogonal projection matrix if and only if ${Q}^{2}=Q$ and ${Q}^{T}=Q.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is an orthogonal projection matrix. Indeed,
${A}^{T}=A$
and

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5} & -\frac{2}{5} \\ -\frac{2}{5} & \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5} & -\frac{2}{5} \\ -\frac{2}{5} & \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 \\ -10 & 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5} & -\frac{2}{5} \\ -\frac{2}{5} & \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =A.\end{aligned}
$$

- $B$ is *not* an orthogonal projection matrix. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{T}\ne B.\end{aligned}
$$

- $C$ is *not* an orthogonal projection matrix. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{T}\ne C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ only."

html:
Question 13
?

Which of the following are orthogonal projection matrices?

A=[15−25−2545],B=[25−353515],C=[12233412].

a
A and C only
b
A only
c
B only
d
C only
e
B and C only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that Q is an orthogonal projection matrix if and only if Q2=Q and QT=Q.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

  • A is an orthogonal projection matrix. Indeed, AT=A and A2=A⋅A=[15−25−2545][15−25−2545]=15[1−2−24]⋅15[1−2−24]=125[1−2−24][1−2−24]=125[5−10−1020]=[15−25−2545]=A.

  • B is not an orthogonal projection matrix. We have BT≠B.

  • C is not an orthogonal projection matrix. We have CT≠C.

Therefore, the correct answer is "A only."
